correctness.rationale: A self-contained proof shows that every binary arch closes exactly at the next available nonoverlapping bit-transition edge. The resulting maximal path-component matching gives the word index. A two-state suffix automaton produces the stated exact trivariate series, and binomial coefficient extraction recovers exact boundary cases and attainable k. An edge-indicator run argument proves the conditional mean; dominated convergence plus a random-subset transposition bounded-difference inequality yields the all-density limit. Independent finite direct-subsequence, greedy, matching DP, full-word histogram, transfer-polynomial, and transition-subset computations passed from the actual standalone verifier path. These finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

The structural matching law and conditional transition-density theorem therefore constitute the candidate beyond what the compared statements imply.

originality.rationale: The greedy arch lemma and the full unrefined binary distribution are previously known and explicitly excluded from the new contribution. The proposed joint law by exact adjacent-transition count, equivalence to a graph maximum matching, and the sharp conditional mean/density statement are not stated by the compared closest complete texts. The strongest known direct comparison gives only the y=1 marginal. There is a residual risk of equivalent path-matching enumeration under graph-theoretic vocabulary.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-parameter path-subgraph matching-number distribution might appear in graph combinatorics under unrelated wording.
A later or uncatalogued treatment may simultaneously track runs and subsequence-universality index.

value.rationale: A natural finite-difference complexity statistic (adjacent bit changes) is coupled exactly to a natural scattered-pattern coverage statistic (subsequence universality). The maximum-matching bridge supplies a structural interpretation, the trivariate generating function classifies all finite lengths and feasible index ranges, and the conditional law of large numbers identifies the typical exact-budget performance at every transition density. This is a motivated infinite-parameter structural and probabilistic result, not just a restatement of the known univariate enumeration.
